correctness.rationale: Averaging squared distances from z=t1+w, w orthogonal 1, over each complete Hamming-weight-s orbit gives d t²+s(1-2t)+||w||². The farthest vertex distance is at least its layer average; a symmetric center t1 realizes equality on every vertex of a given layer. Maximizing in s depends only on a=min S, b=max S because q_s(t) is affine in s. The two-piece strongly convex envelope is uniquely minimized at t=h/d, w=0. Radius²=h(d-h)/d, and the strict affine layer difference identifies only b contacts below d/2, only a above d/2, and every vertex in the crossing case. Works for d=1, singleton S and degenerate polytopes; finite enumeration through d<=8 is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete published general Boolean-polytope minimum-sphere theorem states for ANY V⊂{0,1}^d that its unique minimum-enclosing-ball center is the Euclidean projection of u=(1/2)1 onto P=conv(V), with radius² d/4-||u-c||² and contact vertices exactly the maximizers of <1-2c,v>. Apply it to an S-hypersimplex: permutation-invariance makes that projection diagonal; the available diagonal coordinates are exactly [min S/d,max S/d], hence c=(h/d)1. Radius and all layer contacts then follow immediately. This directly covers every part of the submitted S-hypersimplex result, not merely its ordinary or uniform subclasses.
